title: What Space School Programs Is
definition: Space School Programs: programs preparing students for space.
description:
Space School Programs: programs preparing students for space. This is Future Education & Work at its most ambitious — analog missions research, program logistics engineering and STEM tracks operations converging on a single goal: making program hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Education & Work will decide crew training outcomes this century. Space School Programs is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working program hulls, the larger analog missions vision stalls, and with it, the program logistics systems that depend on it.

t: Real Research Today: Space School Programs
title: Real Research Today: Space School Programs
definition: Today's documented research behind Space School Programs.
description:
The road to Space School Programs is already being paved. Carnegie Mellon's Open Learning Initiative proved adaptive courseware doubles learning rates. Maker education (FabLearn, fab labs) puts fabrication tools in thousands of schools.

The OECD's Learning Compass 2030 defines future-ready competencies for schools. Together these programs form the analog missions foundation that Space School Programs will build on — the program logistics results, the STEM tracks methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as program logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First program hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Space School Programs roadmap.
description:

title: Readiness Estimator: Space School Programs
definition: Estimates Space School Programs readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Space School Programs components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a program hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Space School Programs Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Space School Programs operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Space School Programs installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 15043 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where analog missions monitoring, program logistics redundancy, or STEM tracks maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Space School Programs Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Space School Programs: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Space School Programs — programs preparing students for space.

Phase 1 — Prove (analog missions): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (program logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (STEM tracks): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (crew training): program hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and students-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
